gdp.title: GDP (real, per year)
gdp.formula: GDP = (firm sales + investment + government services) x 12, divided by the price index

parts.label: Investment
parts.note: firms' capital spending this month x 12

parts.label: Government services
parts.note: public works, upkeep and job guarantee pay x 12

gpi.title: GPI (per year)
gpi.formula: GPI = GDP x (1 - Gini) - social cost of carbon x 12 x gross emissions - depletion cost x 12 x depletion

parts.label: Inequality discount
parts.note: GDP x (1 - Gini) takes the Gini share of GDP away

parts.label: Social cost of carbon
parts.note: cost per tonne x 12 x gross emissions this month

parts.label: Depletion of forest and commons
parts.note: cost per unit x 12 x natural capital lost this month

wageShare.title: Wage share
wageShare.formula: Wage share = wages paid to households / GDP (monthly)

profitShare.title: Profit share
profitShare.formula: Profit share = profits of firms making a profit / GDP (monthly)

debtToGdp.title: Public debt / GDP
debtToGdp.formula: Debt / GDP = government debt / annual GDP (nominal); 0 if GDP is not positive

gini.title: Inequality (Gini)
gini.formula: Gini = sum over all pairs of people of |wealth_i - wealth_j| / (2 x people x total wealth); each person holds an equal share of their household's net worth; 0 = equal, 1 = one person has everything

legitimacy.title: Legitimacy
legitimacy.formula: Each month: legitimacy = previous + w1 x (wellbeing - 0.5) - w2 x max(0, unemployment - threshold) - w3 x max(0, Gini - threshold) - w4 x max(0, debt/GDP - 1) - bailout penalty - system-change resistance, kept within 0..1

parts.label: Public debt above one year of GDP
Switching economic system (resistance)
parts.note: only while a system change is under way

terms.label: Public debt above one year of GDP

capitalRatio.title: Bank capital ratio
capitalRatio.formula: Capital ratio = bank equity / loans outstanding (1 when there are no loans). The bank may lend while equity / limit >= loans; headroom = equity / limit - loans

emissions.note: Gross emissions = firms (direct) + households (direct) + power plants. Electricity used by firms and households is counted once, at the plants that burn the fuel, so it is not added again to firms or households. Net = gross minus the forest sink. The month line is the latest month; the turn line adds the months of the latest turn. The fire line shows sink lost to fire and is not a term of the sum.

taxes.label: Income tax
taxes.appliesTo: Wages and salaries households earn (job guarantee and public-works pay included)
taxes.note: Lever key tax_wage. Paid only from what the household has in savings.

taxes.label: Profit tax
taxes.appliesTo: Firm profit before tax (nothing on a loss), before dividends
taxes.baseLabel: firm profit before tax this month ($)
taxes.note: Lobbying can weaken it: the rate in force is the effective rate.

taxes.label: Capital tax
taxes.appliesTo: Households' dividends, rent received and interest received

taxes.label: Wealth tax
taxes.appliesTo: Household net worth above the threshold (annual rate, collected in twelfths)
taxes.note: Annual rate; the realised rate is revenue x 12 over the taxed wealth. Lobbying can weaken it.

taxes.label: Carbon price
taxes.appliesTo: Each firm's footprint: direct emissions plus the emissions of the electricity it uses
taxes.note: A price in dollars per tonne, not a fraction. Lobbying can weaken it.

taxes.label: GST / VAT
taxes.appliesTo: Not modelled: the town has no sales or value-added tax
taxes.note: Adding a sales tax would change prices, demand and the ledger; it is a possible future option.

publicGoods.label: Government purchases of goods
publicGoods.buys: Goods from the Factory, bought with the public spending lever. Split with services by a fixed share; this is derived, the ledger records one purchase line.

publicGoods.label: Government purchases of services
publicGoods.buys: Services from the Shop, the other part of the public spending lever.

publicGoods.label: Public works (upkeep and construction)
publicGoods.buys: Upkeep of roads, public housing, power plants and fire stations, resilience spending and new builds; paid out as wages to households.

publicGoods.label: Job guarantee
publicGoods.buys: Government jobs at the minimum wage for unemployed people who want one.

publicGoods.label: Benefits
publicGoods.buys: Payments to unemployed adults and retired people.

publicGoods.label: Universal basic income
publicGoods.buys: A flat payment to every person.

publicGoods.label: Green investment subsidy
publicGoods.buys: Part of firms' green investment costs.

industry.note: No state shareholding in the current economic systems (Market, Regulated, Co-op): the state's ownership share is 0% for every firm. The state-owned variant exists in the model but no system uses it yet.
